questions.stem: A substance has a high melting point, does not conduct electricity when solid, but does conduct when molten. What type of structure does it have?
questions.explanation: This describes a giant ionic structure. It has a high melting point due to strong electrostatic forces between ions. It does not conduct when solid because the ions are fixed in position, but it conducts when molten because the ions become free to move and carry charge.

questions.stem: Which type of structure would a substance have if it conducts electricity when solid and can be bent without breaking?
questions.explanation: This describes a metallic structure. Metals conduct electricity when solid because they have delocalised electrons that are free to move and carry charge. They can be bent (malleable) because layers of ions can slide over each other while the delocalised electrons maintain the bonding.
